meta.title: Signs of Winter — Set 1
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Comprehension on daylight hours, Earth orbit, and animal preparation in winter.

questions.question: How many seasons are there during the year?
questions.explanation: There are four seasons during the year: spring, summer, autumn, and winter.

questions.question: In France it is winter in December, but in New Zealand it is winter in July.
questions.explanation: True. Because they are in different hemispheres, France and New Zealand experience winter in different months.

questions.question: What are Vanessa and Tom building in the winter?
questions.explanation: The text says: 'Vanessa and Tom are building a snowman. They start by making a huge snowball.'

questions.question: There is very little daylight in winter, so it gets dark early in the evening.
questions.explanation: True. Winter has shorter days and longer nights, meaning it gets dark early.

questions.question: What do pine and fir trees have that stay on them during the winter?
questions.explanation: The text mentions: 'Pine and fir trees have needles. The needles stay on the trees during winter.'

questions.question: Winter happens in the parts of Earth that are _______ from the sun.
questions.explanation: Earth's orbit around the sun brings some parts closer to it, while other parts get farther. Winter happens in the parts farthest from the sun.

questions.question: Many trees are bare in winter because their branches grow thick green leaves.
questions.explanation: False. 'Bare' means their branches do not have any leaves at all in winter.

questions.question: Sort these details based on whether they describe Plants or Animals in winter:
questions.explanation: Needles and leafless branches describe plants. Fur coats and collecting sticks describe animal adaptations.

questions.question: Beavers eat the bark of sticks and logs during the winter.
questions.explanation: True. Beavers collect sticks and logs in autumn and eat the bark during the cold winter.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show how Earth moves:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Earth travels around the sun.' This movement changes the seasons.

questions.question: Why does an American bison's coat grow extra long and thick in winter?
options: To keep it warm in the cold temperature
To help it run faster in deep snow
To hide from other animals in the forest
To collect extra sticks and logs
questions.explanation: The thick and long coat of the bison keeps it warm when the temperature is very cold.

questions.question: Beavers store extra logs in the water near their _______.
questions.hint: A beaver's home made of mud and wood.
questions.explanation: Beavers store logs in the water near their lodges to eat the bark during winter.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe the winter weather:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'The temperature is very cold.' This makes animals grow thick coats.

questions.question: Bobby likes to build a wooden lodge in the water in winter.
questions.explanation: False. In the text, Bobby likes to go sledding in the winter, while beavers build lodges.

questions.question: Based on the text, what is the main cause of the seasons changing on Earth?
options: Earth traveling around the sun, which moves parts of Earth closer or farther from it
Animals moving to warmer places for the winter
Vanessa and Tom making a huge snowman in December
questions.explanation: Seasons change because Earth travels around the sun, causing different parts of the planet to get closer or farther from the sun's warmth.
